Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — PoC scope & GPU tradeoffs (A100 vs H100)

Hi Anna — thanks again for the run-through today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can size a tidy Dedicated PoC for Crestline: 

Summary from the call:
- Primary use case: real-time assistant behind Crestline Support (low-latency chat + async long-form synthesis).
- Expected traffic profile: baseline ~80–120 TPS, occasional spikes to ~250 TPS for high-traffic campaigns; 15% of requests are long-context (>2k tokens) for case summarization.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 350 ms for short chats (under 512 tokens); longer jobs can be async/queued.
- Data controls: VPC peering required; logs retained for 90 days (audit requirement).

Questions we still need from you to finalize sizing: 
1) Can you confirm the average input+output token count for chat messages (short path) and the average tokens for long-context jobs? You mentioned ~150 tokens avg for chats but will confirm.
2) Do you want redundancy across AZs in the PoC (adds cost but reduces impact during maintenance)?
3) Any procurement constraints on specific GPU families? e.g., H100 preferred for high throughput/quantization-sensitive models, A100 for price-performance.

Initial Redwood recommendation (PoC baseline):
- Start: Hybrid Dedicated pool with 2x H100 (80GB) and 4x A100 (40GB) available to the tenant. The H100s handle the heavy long-context and throughput bursts; A100s for steady-state short-chat concurrency.
- Autoscaling policy: maintain baseline of 4 GPU-equivalents; scale to 8 during spikes (burst window 30m, subject to quota).
- Model suggestion: open LLM family (quantized) we tested internally — gives predictable latency at ~200 tokens/req. We'll map exact model to your quality bar once we get example prompts.

Deliverables I can put in the PoC:
- 2-week load-run with your sample traffic (we'll replay crestline_tps_profile.csv you shared)
- Telemetry dashboard access for token-level cost & latency breakdowns
- A short runbook for concurrency knobs and fallback policy to our hosted model if capacity is exhausted

I've attached a draft SOW and the TPS profile we captured in the call. If that looks good, can we lock in a PoC kickoff next week? Proposed kickoff: Mon 27 Jul.

Thanks — Sean

Quick engineering note for the PoC options — high level: 

Option A (A100-first) — Cost-efficient baseline
- Config: 6x A100 40GB equivalent capacity (spread across nodes for AZ resilience).
- Expected steady throughput: ~110–140 TPS for short-chat model (200 token median) with 95th latency ~300–380ms depending on batching.
- Long-context handling: will be queued onto A100s; expect higher tail latency for 3k+ token jobs and reduced concurrency for those requests.
- Pros: better unit cost, simpler procurement.
- Cons: may fail to meet burst headroom without prewarming or temporary burst H100s.

Option B (Hybrid with H100) — Performance-first
- Config: 2x H100 (80GB) + 4x A100 (40GB). H100s preferred for large-context slices and faster kv-cache handling.
- Expected steady throughput: A100s cover baseline 100 TPS; H100s take overflow/long-context jobs, lowering tail latency. 95th for short chats ~250–300ms; long-context jobs complete in ~15–35s depending on token length and model.
- Pros: smoother latency profile under burst and for long-context jobs; less queueing.
- Cons: higher cost; procurement may push back.

PoC proposal: run Option A baseline first for 5 days of replay; if tail metrics show >20% SLA misses on 95th, add on 1–2 H100s and measure delta. This staged approach aligns with procurement preference and gives clear measurement gating.

I'll draft the throughput numbers and expected token-cost table for Vanessa to include in the commercial note.

– Karthik
